prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity landscape desktop website first-viewport comp for a public developer portfolio homepage
Primary request: Create exactly one polished 1536×1024 desktop homepage design for the direction “ANALYST’S WORKING PAPER,” with a visual lineage of financial research workbooks and annotated model printouts. It must unmistakably look like a usable responsive public portfolio website, not a poster, slide, magazine cover, or atmosphere image.
Scene/backdrop: Full-bleed straight-on desktop webpage canvas, no browser chrome, no device mockup, no perspective distortion. Pale paper background #F4F7F5.
Subject: A concise working memo establishing a developer/finance thesis. Use a practical top navigation whose items behave visually like workbook index tabs. The hero’s dominant focal region is a large, inspectable, marked-up figure representing an unnamed financial app project as working evidence: abstract chart traces, interface wireframes, formula fragments, blue ledger ruling, carbon-pencil annotations, chart overlays, registration marks, and margin notes, but NO readable invented numbers, metrics, app name, company name, client, employer, testimonial, or claim. Add a narrow evidence column labeled “GitHub activity,” using restrained contribution-like marks with no numerical claims. Show enough of the second fold below the hero to establish a clear work / project / blog rhythm, with only the permitted proof labels and neutral abstract placeholders.
Style/medium: High-fidelity editorial web UI, rigorous information design, analyst notebook meets software portfolio, warm human annotations over precise grid systems. Flat front-on interface design. Refined typography, strong hierarchy, generous negative space, production-realistic interaction affordances, crisp 1px rules. Avoid generic fintech aesthetics.
Composition/framing: 1536×1024 landscape. Compact header at top. Hero uses an asymmetric editorial grid: clear thesis and CTA on the left, dominant marked-up flagship-app figure across the center, narrow GitHub evidence column at right. The app figure is the single dominant move; all other regions are quiet. At the bottom, reveal approximately 20–25% of the next section to prove ongoing project and blog structure. Keep all content safely within the canvas.
Lighting/mood: Bright diffuse paper-like daylight, cerebral, credible, exploratory, precise, not glossy.
Color palette: paper #F4F7F5, ink #101828, cobalt #174EA6, data lime #B6F23A, signal red #D93D45. Cobalt rules and annotations; lime used sparingly as data highlight; red only as editorial signal marks.
Materials/textures: Subtle recycled paper grain, blue ledger ruling, carbon annotations, translucent chart overlays, index tabs, clipped research-note details; retain clean modern UI legibility.
Text (verbatim, render every item exactly and legibly): Navigation: “HOME”, “PROJECTS”, “ABOUT”, “RESUME”, “CONTACTS”, “BLOG”. Headline: “Developer focused on financial tools.” Supporting line: “I build and write about technology, development, and finance.” Primary action: “Explore my work”. Proof labels: “GitHub activity” and “Financial app project”.
Constraints: Exact visible copy only as specified above; nav must clearly read as navigation, “Explore my work” must clearly read as an actionable button or link; show clear web-page structure and usable alignment; the financial app figure must remain unnamed and schematic; no profile portrait; no logos; no stock photography. Preserve spelling, capitalization, and punctuation of all required text.
Avoid: generic fintech dashboard, bento grid, polished corporate deck, glowing gradients, dark crypto UI, banking app cliché, fake analytics, invented charts with readable values, invented metrics, dates, company names, clients, testimonials, app names, employers, awards, claims, fake article titles, fake body copy, poster composition, browser chrome, watermark, illegible or misspelled required text.
